entries.title: Lightning Labs ships Wavelength on mainnet: bitcoin payments any agent can integrate
entries.summary: Wavelength, Lightning Labs' payments toolkit, opened to everyone on mainnet October 23. An agent can hold a balance and pay for API calls, data feeds or another agent's service in fractions of a cent over Lightning - no card, account, node or channels. wavecli mcp serve exposes the wallet as MCP tool calls; L402 handles pay-per-request APIs.
entries.detail: This is the closest shipping thing to the SatStacker payment lane. It is still alpha: accounts are capped at 300,000 sats (50,000 per VTXO), Lightning payments carry a 0.25% service fee plus routing fees, and stablecoins are only 'coming soon' per Lightning Labs. The custody shape is the interesting part: users hold their own keys with a unilateral exit back to the bitcoin chain, wallet unlock stays on the command line so seeds never cross the agent channel, and receive-only macaroon credentials let an agent get paid with no ability to sign or recover. Funds need a refresh roughly every two weeks, handled automatically while the wallet runs. Fee and cap figures are Lightning Labs' own documentation, checked October 24.

entries.title: Coinbase opens customer accounts to AI agents over MCP
entries.summary: Coinbase announced 'Coinbase is open for AI agents' on October 22: users can connect approved assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Codex CLI and others) through its MCP server to trade crypto, US stocks and derivatives. The user picks which portfolios the agent can access, previews orders before execution, and can disconnect at any time.
entries.detail: Reported by Yahoo Finance / 24/7 Wall St on October 23. The setup is agents.coinbase.com/mcp as a custom MCP server with an approval screen; a September update had already added stocks, ETFs and x402 payments that let agents buy market data from a user's USDC balance. Coinbase's own risk framing matches what this watch keeps repeating: fund only a separate, limited portfolio for agent trading, because the named failure modes are prompt injection, the agent misreading vague instructions, and over-broad permissions. Coinbase has reported no agent revenue so far and gave no usage numbers. Feature claims are Coinbase's; the risk framing is the article's.

entries.status: Disclosed / fixed in the August 18 releases
entries.title: x402 SDK flaw let a malicious API ask an agent's wallet for its full token balance
entries.summary: Security firm V12 disclosed 25 flaws in the x402 payment SDKs, three critical: the default client set no spending limit (a hostile API could request the wallet's full token balance), the TypeScript Solana facilitator accepted token approvals as valid payments, and SIWx login messages were not checked against the site actually contacted. All three were fixed in the August 18 releases, which cap payments at $1 and recognized stablecoins by default.
entries.detail: The uncomfortable part is the disclosure gap: the x402 Foundation published no security advisories and the changelogs do not call the fixes security fixes, so npm audit and PyPI gave no warning to upgrade - teams on releases before 2.23.0 (TS) or 2.25.0 (Python) have to find out some other way. Neither V12 nor the foundation reports any real-world exploit. The design lesson is the SatStacker one: any agent that auto-signs payments needs explicit per-payment budgets, token allowlists and site verification, which is exactly what the fixed clients now ship. Technical claims are V12's as reported by The Hacker News, checked October 24.

sources.label: The Hacker News on the V12 findings

entries.title: An LLM agent searched for trading strategies; a simple heuristic beat it, and the harness was the real hero
entries.summary: Pavel Kazantsev gave DeepSeek V3 forty rounds to propose crypto strategies, scored by a walk-forward harness the model could not touch. A dumb heuristic proposer found +52% net first; the agent's early proposals lost money; its real value was surfacing three silent harness bugs; and its later +123.7% 'win' turned out to be parameter sensitivity, not edge.
entries.detail: The details matter more than the headline. The agent never touched scoring - it proposed, the same judge every hand-built strategy faced decided. Once the space was debugged it genuinely mapped a corner (factor-residual reversion, 40-80 day lookbacks), but the honest ensemble result was +75.8% in-sample with a t-stat around 1.4: not significant. His conclusions read like a checklist for the deterministic-core design: run a heuristic baseline first; the agent is only as honest as the thing that scores it; once a proposer can optimize it will, so watch breadth, not magnitude; average the plateau instead of picking the winner. A personal blog experiment with the author's own caveats, not peer-reviewed research - but unusually rigorous about its own search bias.

entries.title: Binance pushes agent wallets with claimable '.ai' Agent ID names
entries.summary: Binance co-founder Yi He is promoting Agent ID - unique '.ai' names for Binance Wallet's agentic wallet, pitched as an alternative to long 0x addresses. It sits on the August Agent OS platform: MCP integration, isolated agent subaccounts for spot, margin and futures trading, and no external-withdrawal permission for agents.
entries.detail: Neither promo post shows an actual payment or trade completed through the names, so treat this as a naming launch on top of real plumbing. The plumbing is the part worth watching: a dedicated subaccount, isolated from the main account, where the agent can trade but cannot withdraw externally - the exchange-custodied version of the least-privilege pattern Wavelength ships self-custodied. Caveat for a California-based stack: Binance's global platform is not available to US residents, so this is a pattern to study rather than a tool to use. Reported by crypto.news October 20.

entries.status: Live in Grok Bot marketplace / vendor-described guardrails
entries.title: MetaMask Agent Wallet goes live on Grok Bot with wallet-layer guardrails
entries.summary: MetaMask's Agent Wallet is available as a Grok Bot marketplace plugin as of October 28: plain-language requests can check balances, swap and bridge tokens, trade Hyperliquid perps, take Polymarket positions and supply to yield vaults. MetaMask says the wallet is self-custodial with keys in a trusted execution environment, every supported transaction simulated and Blockaid-scanned, and Guard Mode enforcing allowlists plus a rolling 24-hour outflow limit you set, with two-factor approval for anything outside it.
entries.detail: The structurally important detail is where the checks fire: swaps are checked trade by trade, but perp positions are checked only at the Hyperliquid deposit - opening, sizing and closing positions are Hyperliquid-signed actions, so a position well past the outflow limit can open without a wallet-level check. Polymarket order placement is likewise off-chain and outside per-order Guard Mode evaluation. A 'Beast Mode' relaxes interruptions while keeping threat scanning, and eligible transactions carry Transaction Protection coverage up to $10,000 a month. The same mm CLI skill works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other skill-supporting agents. All of this is MetaMask's own documentation, not independent testing. Not investment advice.

sources.label: MetaMask news: Agent Wallet live on Grok Bot (primary)

entries.status: Launched per vendor / MCP private beta
entries.title: Tria launches agentic perp trading with trade-only keys
entries.summary: Tria announced Agentic Trading on October 30: AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor execute Hyperliquid and Decibel perpetual-futures strategies through a user's existing Tria account, authorized through expiring, revocable trade-only keys that cannot withdraw funds. Tria's own documentation qualifies the launch: the MCP server is in access-restricted private beta, and both venues trade real mainnet markets with no testnet target. This is perp execution, not a verified native ZEC/ADA or spot bitcoin-DCA product.
entries.detail: Mechanics per the docs: users mint an HL agent wallet and/or a Decibel delegate keypair from the Tria app; agents place, cancel and modify orders but cannot withdraw. Tria's risk disclosure states trade-only permissions do not prevent trading losses, including liquidation of collateral. The 600,000-user figure and named AI-tool support are vendor claims, and usable availability is gated on private-beta npm access. Also covered in this hub's blockchain chapter. Not investment advice.

entries.title: Stack watch: Freqtrade 2026.10 and Jesse 3.5.4 ship the same day; the rest hold

Freqtrade 2026.10 adds orderbook websocket support, decouples the bot loop from RPC messaging for reliability, moves parameters to per-strategy-instance access, and drops Python 3.11. Jesse 3.5.4 is on PyPI (the repo tags without GitHub releases). Hummingbot stays v2.17.0, Nautilus Trader stays v1.231.0 despite active pushes, Condor still has no tagged releases, lightning-agent-tools has been quiet since May, AgentKit is active without tags, and Turnkey's SDK stays v2026.10.4.

entries.title: Wavelength v0.2.1 hardens the BTC agent-payment rail
entries.summary: Lightning Labs published Wavelength v0.2.1 on October 31. The release validates Ark transaction inputs before accepting out-of-round transfers, repairs VTXO expiry monitoring, rejects excessive refund timelocks before funding pay swaps, and improves swap refunds, unilateral exits and fee-bump recovery. This is payment infrastructure for the SatStacker lane, not a bitcoin accumulation strategy.
entries.detail: Linux builds disable MPTCP listeners by default; the release explicitly says this mitigation does not replace installing a patched kernel. Operators must provide complete, co-signed Ark transaction packages, and applications must treat a zero indexed-expiry deadline as unverified timing. These are maintainer-described fixes, not an independent security audit or evidence of a loss in the wild. The published release body retains draft/signing boilerplate, so this check does not certify every binary signature. Wavelength is a separate repository from lightning-agent-tools; its release should not be inferred from the companion repository's older push date. No software installed, keys connected or funds moved.

entries.title: TaskFuel adds Lightning funding for paid agent tools
entries.summary: A November 4 Stacker News post from the @Alby account announces bitcoin Lightning top-ups for TaskFuel: pay an invoice in sats, credit one prepaid balance, then let an agent discover, price and call paid tools. TaskFuel's own site describes that balance as USD, not a bitcoin wallet.
entries.detail: The post says Lightning top-ups carry half the fee of card top-ups and tool calls have no added markup over provider pricing; these are builder claims, not independently tested pricing. The public site describes allowlisted HTTP-402 APIs and one prepaid USD balance. This is a way to spend sats on research/data/tool access, not native BTC accumulation, a trading strategy, or proof that provider settlement happens in bitcoin. Account funding, refunds and operational protections were not tested. The dated announcement is a community post, rather than an independently verified launch report.

sources.label: November 4 announcement from @Alby on Stacker News

entries.title: Wayfinder adds advanced spot orders through Definitive Flash
entries.summary: CoinMarketCal reporting carried by TradingView quotes Wayfinder's November 6 announcement: its agents support limit, stop-loss, take-profit and trailing-stop orders for spot tokens across 12 chains, powered by Definitive Flash. The announcement says these can be used through the UI, an agent or strategies.
entries.detail: The useful pattern is natural-language orchestration handing off to explicit order types, rather than a model improvising every execution. Scope remains a reported vendor claim: this sweep did not independently test order execution, wallet permissions, fees, fill quality or the chain list. Twelve-chain spot support does not establish native bitcoin settlement, a BTC DCA workflow or a tested SatStacker implementation. Stops and trailing stops do not guarantee a fill or cap loss during gaps and low liquidity. Not investment advice.

sources.label: TradingView / CoinMarketCal report quoting the announcement
